name: Shillong
description: Capital city of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills district. Known as the 'Scotland of the East', it sits at about 1,500 m elevation with colonial architecture, markets, educational institutions, and access to nearby waterfalls and peaks.
facts: Capital and largest city of Meghalaya
HQ of East Khasi Hills district
Connected by road to Guwahati (about 100 km)

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Stunning turquoise waterfall near Amlarem in West Jaintia Hills. Cascades into a clear natural pool amid lush forests and limestone cliffs, popular for swimming, photography, and short treks.
facts: Turquoise plunge pool ideal for swimming with life jackets

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest collection of ancient monoliths in the Khasi-Jaintia Hills, featuring menhirs and dolmens erected between the 16th and 19th centuries by Jaintia kings and clans. Includes the tallest menhir around 8 metres high.

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: 600-year-old Hindu temple and one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, dedicated to Goddess Durga (Jayanti). Located in Nartiang village, it draws pilgrims especially during Durga Puja.

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Man-made historical lake near Jowai, also called Pung Sajar Nangli. Created according to legend by a rebel general and his followers; popular for picnics and boating amid pine forests.
facts: Legend of Sajar Nangli digging it overnight

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Crystal-clear river at the India-Bangladesh border near Dawki town. Famous for transparent waters where boats appear to float, with a historic 1932 suspension bridge and boating.

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Village upstream on the Umngot River from Dawki, offering quieter crystal-clear waters, camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, and community eco-tourism.

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Multi-tiered waterfall near Jowai on the Shillong-Jowai highway. Cascades over rocky cliffs amid paddy fields and forests; accessible with a short walk.
facts: Popular local picnic and photo spot

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered waterfall near Shkentalang/Jarain in West Jaintia Hills, meaning 'Paradise' in Jaintia. Drops into a turquoise pool after a moderate forest trek.
facts: Name means Paradise in local language

name: Jowai Town
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district, a cultural hub for the Pnar/Jaintia people. Gateway to local markets, Syntu Ksiar, and nearby waterfalls and lakes on the Myntdu River plateau.

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park about 8 km from Jowai featuring a sacred grove and panoramic views of the Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu River. Developed for eco-tourism with walking trails.

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Scenic riverside meadow on the Myntdu River near Jowai, meaning 'Golden Flower'. Historic site linked to freedom fighter U Kiang Nangbah; popular for picnics, fishing, and suspension bridge views.
facts: Site associated with U Kiang Nangbah
Suspension bridge and fish sanctuary nearby

name: Thlu Muwi
description: Historic stone bridge about 16 km from Jowai on the road to Dawki, built by local craftsmen under Jaintia kings for monsoon crossing. Adjacent to Muwi Waterfalls.
facts: Built for king's passage during monsoons
